code.summary: Whether a reply ends by asking something, even with an example after the question mark.

code.name: render

code.summary: Text as ⏺ Markdown, tool calls as ⏺ Name(arg), results as ⎿ first line (+N lines), errors red (by flag or an ERROR: prefix), thinking hidden. Updates state: step, asked, model.

code.name: short_name
code.signature: def short_name(name: str, prefix: str='') -> str

code.name: status_label
code.signature: def status_label(state: dict, started: float) -> str
code.summary: '✻ Running scaffold_get… 7s · ctrl-c to interrupt' for console.status().

code.name: create_new
code.signature: def create_new(folder: Path, stem: str, text: str, suffix: str='.md', limit: int=99) -> Path
code.summary: Create folder/stem.md, or stem-2.md, stem-3.md ... never overwriting or following a link.

code.name: inside
code.signature: def inside(dest: Path, rel: str) -> Path
code.summary: The path for `rel` under `dest`. Refuses absolute paths, `..`, any symbolic link on the way (dest/.git -> elsewhere redirects everything beneath it), and anything resolving outside dest.

code.name: write_tree
code.signature: def write_tree(dest: Path, files: dict[str, str]) -> list[Path]
code.summary: Write {relative path: text} under dest, checking every path before writing any.

code.name: Ask
code.signature: Ask = Callable[[str, dict[str, Any], Any], Awaitable[Any]]

code.name: CortexSession
code.summary: Connects on the first turn. Never sets allowed_tools (Cortex treats it as an exclusive allowlist); read-only tools are approved in the permission callback, everything else goes to `ask`, and with no `ask` it is denied.

code.name: TurnStalled
code.summary: Cortex sent nothing for longer than the idle timeout; the turn was interrupted.

code.name: error_result
code.summary: Cortex drops is_error for in-process tools, so the text says ERROR first as well.

code.name: ParseError
code.summary: A line that is not a valid dotenv assignment.

code.name: parse_line
code.signature: def parse_line(line: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None
code.summary: Return (name, value) for an assignment, or None for a blank or comment line.

code.name: read_env
code.signature: def read_env(filename: str) -> tuple[dict[str, str], list[str]]
code.summary: Read a dotenv file. Returns its variables and one error line per unparseable line.

code.name: SchemaError
code.summary: The schema file cannot be read or is malformed.

code.name: check_value
code.signature: def check_value(variable: Variable, value: str) -> str | None
code.summary: Return what is wrong with value for its type, or None if it fits.

code.name: git
code.summary: Run git in repo; raise GitError with its message on failure. Returns stdout.

code.name: hook_script
code.signature: def hook_script(marker: str, command: list[str], fallback: str='') -> str
code.summary: A POSIX hook that runs a kept-aside earlier hook first, then `command`. The command's first word is found on PATH, else at `fallback`; if neither exists it says so instead of skipping silently. Every embedded value is shell-quoted.

code.name: init_own_repo
code.summary: git init repo if needed, then make sure git resolves it to itself and not to a parent repo.

code.name: install_hook
code.signature: def install_hook(repo: Path, name: str, script: str, marker: str) -> str | None
code.summary: Install `script` as hook `name` where git runs hooks. An existing hook that is not ours (no `marker` line) is kept as <name>.local, which our script runs first. Returns why it could not install, or None.

code.name: pointer_problems
code.signature: def pointer_problems(text: str, versions: dict[str, int]) -> list[str]
code.summary: What is wrong with the pointers, given {id: current version}: unknown ids, impossible pins.

code.name: pointers
code.signature: def pointers(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, int | None]]
code.summary: (id, pinned version or None) for every pointer in prose.

code.name: check_out_dir
code.signature: def check_out_dir(out: Path, protect: list[Path], marker: str=MARKER) -> Path
code.summary: The resolved output directory, or ValueError when emptying it could delete something: it is or contains a protected path, home or the root, or it holds files that are not a previous build carrying the marker.

code.name: mark_out_dir
code.signature: def mark_out_dir(out: Path, marker: str=MARKER) -> None

code.name: render_scaffold
code.signature: def render_scaffold(canon_root: Path, entry: dict[str, Any], name: str, purpose: str, test_cmd: str | None=None, lint_cmd: str | None=None) -> dict[str, str]

code.name: scaffold_digest
code.signature: def scaffold_digest(canon_root: Path, entry: dict[str, Any]) -> str
code.summary: SCAFFOLD.md, then each template's path under the scaffold dir and its bytes, as build_index.py hashes.

code.name: check_one_line
code.signature: def check_one_line(label: str, value: str) -> None
code.summary: Raise ValueError unless value is one line of printable text.

code.name: check_project_name
code.signature: def check_project_name(name: str, max_len: int=41) -> str
code.summary: Lowercase words joined by single dashes, whose package name imports. Returns the package name.

code.name: fill_template
code.signature: def fill_template(text: str, values: dict[str, str]) -> str
code.summary: Replace {{key}} in one pass, so a value containing {{other}} stays literal. Unknown keys stay.

code.name: json_literal
code.summary: A string literal valid in JSON, Python, TOML and YAML (double-quoted) at once. Raw Unicode is kept (TOML rejects JSON's surrogate escapes); DEL is escaped (TOML and YAML refuse it raw).

code.name: browse
code.signature: async def browse(title: str, items: list[Item], *, visible: int=10, width: int=S.DESIGN_WIDTH) -> str | None
code.summary: Returns the chosen Item.value, or None on Esc / Ctrl-C.

code.name: form
code.signature: async def form(title: str, fields: list[Field], footer: Callable[[dict[str, str]], str], validate: Callable[[dict[str, str]], tuple[str, str] | None], width: int=S.DESIGN_WIDTH) -> dict[str, str] | None
code.summary: Every field on one screen, already filled with a suggestion, inside a square frame. Tab/↓ and Shift-Tab/↑ move, Enter submits from any field. Labels sit on the LABEL_W grid.

code.name: pick
code.signature: async def pick(title: str, options: list[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> str | None
code.summary: options: (value, label, description). ↑/↓ or a digit to move, Enter to choose.

code.name: prompt_frame
code.signature: def prompt_frame(tag: str, text: str, width: int) -> list[tuple[str, str]]
code.summary: The three static rows of a prompt frame, as prompt_toolkit fragments: what `prompt_line` draws live, and what the caller reprints once the line is accepted. Cortex Code's box: the terminal's width, rounded corners, the session tag at the right of the top rule.

code.name: prompt_line
code.signature: async def prompt_line(tag: str, *, completer=None, history=None, toolbar: Callable[[], list] | None=None, width: int | None=None) -> str
code.summary: One line of input inside a closed frame the width of the terminal, the session tag on its top rule, the status band under it, the `/` menu dropping below, ↑↓ for history (or the menu when it is open), Tab to complete, Enter to accept. Raises KeyboardInterrupt on ctrl-c and EOFError on ctrl-d with an

code.name: resize_safe
code.summary: Give an Application the resize behaviour above. prompt_toolkit 3.0 registers `_on_resize` as its SIGWINCH handler when the app runs, so the instance attribute is what gets called.

code.name: PromptEcho
code.summary: The accepted frame as a renderable: drawn at the console's width each time it is printed, so the repaint after a resize fits the new width instead of re-wrapping a fixed line.

code.name: agent_lines
code.signature: def agent_lines(c: Console, body: RenderableType) -> None
code.summary: ● on the first line, │ on the rest; body may be Markdown. Wraps under col 3.

code.name: banner
code.signature: def banner(version: str, facts: list[tuple[str, str]], hints: list[str], path: str, tagline: str, w: int=DESIGN_WIDTH, art: list[Text] | None=None, name: str='ds-next') -> list[Text]
code.summary: Two-pane frame shown once: the mark and word-mark left, facts right, path on a footer row. `name` is the product's word-mark, in the title and under the mark.

code.name: error
code.signature: def error(what: str, fix: str='') -> list[Text]
code.summary: Red only on the line that failed; the fix follows in dim.

code.name: frame
code.signature: def frame(title: Text | str, rows: list[Text | None], *, kind: str='input', keys: Text | None=None, w: int=DESIGN_WIDTH, prefix: Text | None=None) -> list[Text]
code.summary: Square frame, exact width. kind = input (dim edge) | approval (warn edge). `prefix` is printed before every line (the rail, inside a turn).

code.name: labelled

code.summary: MASCOT as 10 Rich lines of ▀▄█: top pixel = foreground, bottom pixel = background.

code.name: outcome
code.signature: def outcome(kind: str, subject: str, detail: str='') -> Text
code.summary: kind in ok|warn|err — closes a block, never opens one. No rail: local commands are flat.

code.name: prompt_box
code.signature: def prompt_box(tag: str, text: str, w: int) -> list[Text]
code.summary: The prompt frame, three rows at width w: Cortex Code's box, rounded, the session tag at the right of the top rule. `widgets.prompt_frame` draws the same rows live; this is the static print once a line is accepted.

code.name: pt_style
code.summary: The same roles for prompt_toolkit (prompt, completion menu, widgets).

code.name: result
code.signature: def result(first: str, more: int=0, *, error: bool=False, key: str='ctrl-o') -> Text

code.name: run
code.signature: def run(tool: str, arg: str='') -> Text

code.name: session_rule
code.signature: def session_rule(tag: str, w: int=DESIGN_WIDTH) -> Text
code.summary: The top rule of the prompt frame alone.

code.name: status_label
code.signature: def status_label(step: str, secs: int) -> str
code.summary: Markup for console.status: the one live line, redrawn in place.

code.name: theme
code.summary: Rich Theme for this terminal. DS_THEME=light|dark picks the ramp.

code.name: toolbar
code.signature: def toolbar(left: str, right: str, w: int) -> list[tuple[str, str]]
code.summary: prompt_toolkit bottom_toolbar fragments: one quiet band, facts left, context right.
